# Observa — Official Agent & Integration Guide (llms-full.txt)

Single self-contained guide for humans and AI coding agents. Read this before
using or building on Observa. If you are an AI agent asked to implement a
trading strategy, follow the agent rules in section N.

## A. What Observa is

Observa is a deterministic, bar-based backtesting engine for Python trading
strategies. One canonical Rust Engine replays market data bar by bar and
records an ordered event history: what the strategy saw, which orders it
created (and whether they filled/pended/rejected/expired), which exact
position opened and closed, why SL/TP fired and at what price, and what
happened to balance and equity. Observa then replays that history visually so
users can inspect WHY a backtest behaved as it did.

Product principle: the goal is the end of blind trust. The frontend and
Python layer never recompute fills, P&L, SL/TP outcomes, or position pairing;
they are views of the canonical Engine result.

## B. Installation

Private MVP: distributed as an official wheel attached to a private GitHub
Release — NOT from PyPI.

WARNING: do not `pip install observa`. The public PyPI name `observa` is an
unrelated project. Install the official wheel by URL from the private-MVP
GitHub Release:

    python -m pip install "https://github.com/ErickNgumo/observa/releases/download/observa-0.1.1-private-mvp/observa-0.1.1-cp310-abi3-manylinux_2_34_x86_64.whl"

SHA-256 of this exact private-MVP wheel: `9cb10ee386c41b6b8fe5b0ba553894d4a7ff3cafb74ff69b83ae0d3a65a26cf8` (optional check;
not required for basic use).

Real-data examples also need: `python -m pip install yfinance pandas`.

Verified: Linux x86_64 (glibc >= 2.34), CPython 3.13; abi3 metadata supports
Python >= 3.10. No Rust/Cargo/Maturin required at runtime. Building a wheel
is a contributor task, not user onboarding.

Notebook users: if Observa was installed/replaced while a notebook kernel
was running, RESTART the kernel before importing (a running kernel may still
hold the unrelated PyPI 'observa' module in memory).

Verify you imported the correct package:

    import observa
    print(observa.__version__)   # 0.1.1
    print(observa.__file__)      # .../site-packages/observa/__init__.py
    print(hasattr(observa, "Config"), hasattr(observa, "run"))  # True True

## C. Strategy contract

A strategy is a plain Python class with three lifecycle methods:

    class MyStrategy:
        def initialize(self, params=None): ...
        def on_bar(self, bar, portfolio, history): ...
        def teardown(self): ...

- `initialize(params)` — called once before the first bar with the resolved
  parameters dict (empty dict when none configured).
- `on_bar(bar, portfolio, history)` — called once per closed bar, in
  chronological order. `history` contains strictly earlier bars only (no
  lookahead). Return a list of signal dicts (empty list = do nothing).
- `teardown()` — called once after the last bar; raising here fails the run.
- Any Python exception in a callback fails the run with the message. It is
  never silently treated as "no signal".

The canonical bundled sample class lives in
`observa.samples.sample_strategy.SampleEma`.

## D. bar / portfolio / position fields (exact)

bar: read-only dict with keys `timestamp` (RFC 3339 string), `open`, `high`,
`low`, `close`, `volume` (float or None).

portfolio: read-only dict with keys `balance`, `equity`, `used_margin`,
`free_margin`, `has_open_position`, `open_positions` (list of position dicts),
`unrealised_pnl`.

position dict: keys `position_id` (and alias `ticket`), `symbol`,
`direction` ("Buy"/"Sell"), `quantity` (alias `size`), `entry_price`,
`stop_loss`, `take_profit`, `unrealized_pnl`.

Close positions ONLY by exact `position_id`/`ticket`. There is no implicit
FIFO close.

## E. Signals

`on_bar` returns a list of signal dicts.

Direction + optional order type and protective levels:

    {"direction": "buy",  "size": 1.0}                                  # MARKET buy
    {"direction": "sell", "size": 1.0}                                  # MARKET sell
    {"direction": "buy",  "size": 1.0, "order_type": "limit", "price": 1.05,
     "sl": 1.02, "tp": 1.10}                                            # LIMIT buy
    {"direction": "sell", "size": 1.0, "order_type": "stop", "price": 1.10}
                                                                        # STOP sell
    {"direction": "close", "size": pos["size"], "ticket": pos["position_id"]}

Rules:
- direction: "buy" | "sell" | "close".
- MARKET is the default order_type.
- LIMIT/STOP use the `price` field as their trigger/limit price.
- `sl` / `tp` are optional protective levels on entries.
- Python specifies intent. The Rust Engine determines triggering, fill
  timing, spread/slippage, and P&L. Do NOT implement execution.

## E2. Strategy annotations (drawings) — show what the strategy saw

A human may never read your generated strategy code. Annotations are how the
replay explains it. They are **descriptive only**: they never affect orders,
fills, SL/TP, margin, portfolio, metrics or event ordering.

Return them alongside signals (a plain signal list still works):

    return {
        "signals": [...],
        "drawings": [
            {"id": "ema_20", "type": "series", "value": ema20,
             "color": "#58a6ff", "label": "EMA 20"},
        ],
    }

Every drawing has a stable `id` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$`), an optional
`action` (`add` default | `update` | `remove`), and one `type`.
Colours are `#RRGGBB` / `#RRGGBBAA`; `width` is 1|2|3. Timestamps must be real
bar timestamps (`bar["timestamp"]`). At most 256 instructions per bar.

A malformed drawing FAILS the run with `exc.code` (never silently dropped):
DRAWING_TYPE_INVALID, DRAWING_FIELD_MISSING, DRAWING_VALUE_INVALID,
DRAWING_ID_INVALID, DRAWING_ACTION_INVALID, DRAWING_PANE_INVALID,
DRAWING_TIME_INVALID, DRAWING_REFERENCE_INVALID, DRAWING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

### Types

    # continuous per-bar value: same id every bar, one point per bar
    {"id": "ema_20", "type": "series", "value": ema20,
     "series_type": "line",      # line | histogram
     "line_style": "solid",      # solid | dashed | dotted
     "width": 1, "color": "#58a6ff",
     "pane": "price",            # price | separate
     "label": "EMA 20"}

    # horizontal level (POC/VAH/VAL/support/resistance) — extended automatically
    {"id": "poc", "type": "hline", "price": 1.0972,
     "color": "#d29922", "line_style": "dashed", "width": 1, "label": "POC"}

    # straight segment: x1/y1/x2/y2 ALL required (no infinite rays)
    {"id": "trend_1", "type": "line", "x1": t1, "y1": 1.0950, "x2": t2, "y2": 1.0975,
     "color": "#8957e5", "line_style": "solid", "width": 1}

    # price zone; time_end=None extends right as replay advances
    {"id": "zone_1", "type": "rectangle", "time_start": t1, "time_end": None,
     "price_top": 1.0990, "price_bot": 1.0981,
     "color": "#3fb950", "opacity": 0.14, "border": "#3fb950", "label": "FVG"}

    # time window (session/news/research) — no price semantics
    {"id": "london", "type": "region", "time_start": t1, "time_end": t2,
     "color": "#58a6ff", "opacity": 0.10, "label": "London"}

    # strategy marker (signal/anomaly); NOT a substitute for execution markers
    {"id": "sig_1", "type": "marker", "time": t1,
     "position": "below",        # above | below
     "shape": "arrow_up",        # circle | square | arrow_up | arrow_down
     "color": "#3fb950", "text": "long condition true"}

    # text callout
    {"id": "note_1", "type": "label", "time": t1, "price": 1.0980,
     "text": "RSI 27", "color": "#f85149",
     "position": "below"}        # above | below | left | right

### Rules

- `series`: emit one instruction per bar with the SAME id. `value: null` (or
  not emitting) is a GAP — never 0, never interpolated. Use gaps for warm-up.
  `update` on a series is invalid; `remove` stops the series.
- Lifecycle is strategy-driven: `{"id": "zone_1", "action": "remove"}` when a
  zone is filled/invalidated. `update` replaces an existing id (same type).
- Use `pane: "separate"` for values on a different scale (z-score, spread,
  RSI-like). Use `pane: "price"` for overlays (EMA, VWAP, bands).
- A shaded band is just three series (upper/mid/lower); there is no band type.
- Execution markers are Observa-owned; do not emit markers to fake fills.
- `style` is a deprecated ALIAS for `line_style` (it IS honoured).
  `persist` / `fill_price` / `extend` / `bg_color` are accepted but IGNORED —
  they have no effect. Do not use any of them in new strategies.

### Recipes

    # EMA / VWAP overlay
    {"id": "ema_20", "type": "series", "value": ema20, "color": "#58a6ff", "label": "EMA 20"}
    {"id": "vwap",   "type": "series", "value": vwap,  "color": "#d29922", "label": "VWAP"}

    # ±2σ bands = three series (no fill primitive needed)
    {"id": "bb_up", "type": "series", "value": mid + 2*sd, "color": "#58a6ff", "label": "+2σ"}
    {"id": "bb_dn", "type": "series", "value": mid - 2*sd, "color": "#58a6ff", "label": "-2σ"}

    # POC / VAH / VAL
    {"id": "poc", "type": "hline", "price": poc, "color": "#d29922", "label": "POC"}

    # z-score on its own pane
    {"id": "zscore", "type": "series", "value": z, "pane": "separate",
     "color": "#8957e5", "label": "z-score"}

    # FVG: add on the gap bar, remove when price trades back in
    {"id": "fvg_1", "type": "rectangle", "time_start": bar["timestamp"], "time_end": None,
     "price_top": gap_high, "price_bot": gap_low, "color": "#3fb950", "opacity": 0.14}
    {"id": "fvg_1", "action": "remove"}

Full contract with examples: `docs/STRATEGY_API.md` (Strategy annotations).

## F. Explicit-ticket closes

Strong rule: never invent FIFO close behavior. To close a position, always
supply the exact `position_id` obtained from `portfolio["open_positions"]`.
Multiple positions (including long + short on one symbol) are supported.

## G. Data requirements

Accepted inputs: CSV path, list of bar dicts, or DataFrame-like object
(duck-typed via `.to_dict("records")`).

CSV columns, in order:

    timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume

`volume` is optional. Timestamp must parse as RFC 3339 or
`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+00:00` (UTC). Bars must be strictly chronological.
Per-bar validation: open/high/low/close must be internally consistent
(high >= max(open, close), low <= min(open, close)). Observa does not invent
missing candles.

Bundled deterministic sample: `observa.sample_data_path()` returns a CSV path.

## H. Configuration

`observa.Config(...)` public fields (defaults in parentheses):

    starting_balance (10000.0), currency ("USD"), leverage (100.0),
    symbol ("EURUSD"), base_currency ("EUR"), quote_currency ("USD"),
    contract_size (100000.0), price_decimals (5), tick_size (None),
    pip_size (None), min_quantity (0.01), max_quantity (100.0),
    quantity_step (0.01), fill_mode (NEXT_BAR_OPEN), spread (0.0002),
    slippage (0.0001), commission (0.0), commission_mode (PER_SIDE),
    commission_rate_per_unit (0.0), interval ("1d"), order_model (dict),
    params (dict), strategy_name (None), strategy_source (None),
    dataset_source (None)

Constants: observa.MARKET/LIMIT/STOP, BUY/SELL/CLOSE,
BAR_CLOSE/NEXT_BAR_OPEN, PER_SIDE/ROUND_TRIP.

CRITICAL: set `dataset_source` to the data path when replay candles are
required (candle recovery in replay verifies that file against the recorded
dataset hash).

## I. Execution semantics (exact)

- BAR_CLOSE fill mode: MARKET generated while observing completed bar N fills
  at bar N's close.
- NEXT_BAR_OPEN: MARKET generated on bar N fills at bar N+1's open.
- LIMIT/STOP created after observing bar N cannot retroactively fill using
  bar N's range; they rest and start evaluating on future bars.
- Spread is applied half on each side of the market reference; market-style
  executions receive adverse slippage.
- SL/TP attach to a position at fill and are Engine-evaluated.
- Protective chronology: a position opened at bar OPEN is eligible for
  same-bar protective processing; a position opened intrabar (resting
  LIMIT/STOP) or at BAR_CLOSE becomes eligible the NEXT bar (full OHLC range
  may contain prices that occurred before the entry).
- Gaps: an SL cannot execute at the pre-gap price if the market opens through
  it; it fills at the canonical market reference with applicable adjustments.
- Same-bar ambiguity (both SL and TP reachable in one OHLC bar, no resolving
  opening gap): the Engine applies SL-first. This is a deterministic
  convention, not a claim about the true intrabar path.
- No lookahead: history excludes the current bar.
- Open positions are not force-closed at dataset end; unrealised P&L remains
  in final equity (balance != equity when positions remain open).

## J. Persistence

`observa.run(..., output="dir")` (or `result.save("dir")`) writes:

    run.json       what produced the run (config + identities/hashes)
    events.jsonl   authoritative history (one canonical event per line)
    metrics.json   derived statistics (never authoritative)

The run directory is create-only: writing to an existing directory raises
FileExistsError.

## K. Replay

Running a backtest and launching replay are two separate actions. Replay a
persisted run with the installed package:

    observa replay <run-dir> [--port <port>]

The CLI binds a free port automatically and prints the exact URL it bound
(e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:42689`); it never opens a browser and never picks a
fixed default port. `--port N` is strict: if N is taken the CLI prints a
one-line error and exits 2.

The one canonical programmatic entry point is:

    observa.replay(run_dir_or_result, *, port=None, block=True,
                   open_browser=False)

* `block=True` (default) serves until interrupted and prints the URL.
* `block=False` returns a `ReplayServer` immediately: read `server.url`,
  `server.port`, `server.run_dir`, `server.is_running`; call `server.stop()`
  (idempotent) or use it as a context manager. Notebooks and coding agents
  should prefer this and stop the server when done.
* `port=None` binds port 0 so the OS picks a free port — never race or
  pre-inspect ports yourself. An explicit busy port raises `OSError` with
  `exc.code == "REPLAY_PORT_IN_USE"` and `exc.details["port"]`; it does NOT
  fall back to another port.
* A `RunResult` is accepted only when persisted (`output=` on
  `observa.run(...)` or `result.save(dir)`); otherwise `ValueError` with
  `exc.code == "REPLAY_RUN_NOT_PERSISTED"`. Replay only needs the run
  artifacts (`run.json` + `events.jsonl`).

Replay derives all displayed state from canonical events; the chart library is
bundled (offline). If candles cannot be recovered (dataset_source missing or
dataset hash mismatch), the page shows a notice and events/orders/account
still replay.

### K.1 Reading results without replay

    result.summary()          # live result -> one JSON-serializable dict
    observa.run_summary(run_dir)   # persisted run -> dict from run.json/metrics.json

`summary()` keys (exactly): `status`, `artifact_dir`, `total_bars`,
`trades`, `open_positions`, `final_balance`, `final_equity`, `events`,
`metrics`, `dataset_source`, `run_schema_version`. It duplicates no arrays,
so it is cheap for an agent to read repeatedly. `run_summary()` works for runs
produced by any process and reports `status="failed"` plus `error` for a
failed run (`metrics` is `None`, `trades` is `None`).

### K.2 Machine-readable error codes

Observa raises ordinary built-in exceptions and attaches `.code` (string) and
`.details` (dict) instead of requiring message parsing:

    try:
        observa.replay(run_dir, port=7878)
    except OSError as exc:
        exc.code                     # "REPLAY_PORT_IN_USE"
        exc.details                  # {"port": 7878}
        observa.error_code(exc)      # helper; None for uncoded exceptions

Codes: `CONFIG_INVALID`, `DATA_INVALID`, `DATA_FILE_NOT_FOUND`,
`STRATEGY_ERROR`, `ENGINE_ERROR`, `RUN_OUTPUT_EXISTS`, `RUN_PERSIST_FAILED`,
`RUN_DIR_NOT_FOUND`, `RUN_ARTIFACTS_INVALID`, `REPLAY_RUN_NOT_FOUND`,
`REPLAY_ARTIFACTS_INVALID`, `REPLAY_PORT_IN_USE`, `REPLAY_PORT_INVALID`,
`REPLAY_RUN_NOT_PERSISTED`.

Do NOT parse exception messages; switch on `exc.code`. Do NOT wrap a coded
exception in a new exception — that discards the code.

### K.3 Rejections are events, not exceptions

An invalid SL/TP, an oversized quantity, or insufficient margin is NOT an
exception. The order is rejected in the canonical engine and appears as an
`order_rejected` event in `result.events`; the run completes normally. Check
events for rejection reasons (e.g. category/reason fields) instead of
catching exceptions.

## L. Complete working examples

Quickstart A (bundled sample):

    import observa
    from observa.samples.sample_strategy import SampleEma

    data = observa.sample_data_path()
    config = observa.Config(
        fill_mode=observa.NEXT_BAR_OPEN,
        spread=0.0002, slippage=0.0001,
        commission=7.0, commission_mode=observa.ROUND_TRIP,
        interval="15m",
        dataset_source=data,
    )
    result = observa.run(SampleEma(), data, config=config, output="runs/sample")
    print(result.final_balance, result.final_equity, len(result.trades))
    print(result.summary())   # cheap machine-readable status/metrics dict

SMA crossover (20/50), bundled sample:

    import observa

    class SmaCross:
        def __init__(self):
            self.closes = []
        def initialize(self, params=None):
            params = params or {}
            self.fast = int(params.get("fast", 20))
            self.slow = int(params.get("slow", 50))
            self.closes = []
        def on_bar(self, bar, portfolio, history):
            self.closes.append(bar["close"])
            if len(self.closes) < self.slow + 1:
                return []
            fast = sum(self.closes[-self.fast:]) / self.fast
            slow = sum(self.closes[-self.slow:]) / self.slow
            prev_fast = sum(self.closes[-self.fast-1:-1]) / self.fast
            prev_slow = sum(self.closes[-self.slow-1:-1]) / self.slow
            if prev_fast <= prev_slow and fast > slow and not portfolio["has_open_position"]:
                return [{"direction": "buy", "size": 1.0}]
            if prev_fast >= prev_slow and fast < slow and portfolio["has_open_position"]:
                pos = portfolio["open_positions"][0]
                return [{"direction": "close", "size": pos["size"], "ticket": pos["position_id"]}]
            return []
        def teardown(self):
            pass

    data = observa.sample_data_path()
    config = observa.Config(fill_mode=observa.BAR_CLOSE, spread=0.0, slippage=0.0,
                            commission=0.0, params={"fast": 20, "slow": 50},
                            dataset_source=data)
    result = observa.run(SmaCross(), data, config=config, output="runs/sma")
    print(result.final_balance, len(result.trades), len(result.events))

Quickstart B (real data, one self-contained file):
`examples/ema_observa.py` — downloads intraday EUR/USD via yfinance,
normalizes/validates columns, saves the CSV to an ABSOLUTE path, runs an EMA
crossover, persists to a unique timestamped run directory (persistence is
create-only, so rerunning never overwrites), prints results and the replay
command.

Runnable example files: examples/quickstart.py (A), examples/ema_observa.py
(B), examples/rsi_mean_reversion.py.

## M. Common mistakes

- Installing the unrelated PyPI "observa" package. Always install this wheel
  and verify observa.__file__.
- Omitting `dataset_source`, then wondering why replay has no candles.
- Closing a position without an explicit `ticket` (or assuming FIFO).
- Using the current bar in history-based indicators (lookahead).
- Reimplementing fills/spread/slippage/SL-TP/P&L in Python — the Engine owns
  execution.
- Writing independent portfolio P&L math in the strategy or frontend.
- Wrong CSV columns/order or non-chronological timestamps.
- Pre-scanning for a "free port" or assuming port 7878: pass `port=None`
  (default) and read `server.port`/`server.url` instead.
- Calling `observa.replay(result)` on an unpersisted result
  (`REPLAY_RUN_NOT_PERSISTED`) instead of passing `output="dir"` to
  `observa.run(...)`.
- Leaving a non-blocking replay server running in a notebook; call
  `server.stop()`.
- Parsing exception messages for replay/CLI failures instead of reading
  `exc.code`/`exc.details`.
- Treating an order rejection (bad SL/TP, oversized size, insufficient
  margin) as an exception: it is an `order_rejected` event in
  `result.events` and the run completes.

## N. Agent rules

When asked to use Observa:

1. Use the Observa Python API.
2. Do not implement an independent backtesting engine.
3. Do not calculate fills manually.
4. Do not calculate portfolio P&L manually.
5. Do not infer SL/TP outcomes yourself.
6. Use the canonical Engine.
7. Close positions using explicit tickets.
8. Set dataset_source if replay candles are required.
9. Persist the run.
10. Give the user the replay command.
11. For notebooks/agents prefer `observa.replay(run_dir, block=False)` and
    call `server.stop()`; read `server.url` for the actual port.
12. Read results with `result.summary()` / `observa.run_summary(dir)` instead
    of walking full arrays; branch on `exc.code`, never on messages.
13. State assumptions when natural-language strategy rules are ambiguous.
14. Do not claim success unless the code actually ran when execution access exists.

When implementing a user trading strategy: do not modify the Observa engine.
When implementing Observa itself: follow repository architecture and tests
(AGENTS.md).
